title: v1 chat: unify stop propagation and robust tool-call handshake for streamed responses
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: customers using the /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported inconsistent stop handling and truncated toolcall exchanges when streaming responses and falling back across model variants. This PR unifies parameter normalization for stop arrays/sentinels, ensures logprobs and stop signals are propagated deterministically through streaming envelopes, and introduces a resilient tool-call handshake/resume protocol to avoid lost tool outputs in intermediate reconnections.

What this changes (single continuous description): canonicalize v1 chat params: introduce a single param-normalizer that accepts legacy stop formats (string, array, special tokens) and produces an internal stop-set representation used by both batch and streaming paths; coerce role aliases and preserve role metadata when mapping between adapter layers; implement stop-propagation: stops are now evaluated at token-generation and stream-framing layers with consistent precedence (explicit stop list > stop weight heuristics > model-inferred EOS) so clients see matching stop points between sync and streaming responses; logprobs envelope: add compact logprob delta messages emitted on the stream with clear token indices and an explicit final logprob frame for non-streamed fallback; tool-call handshake/resume: new two-way preflight step in the stream (TOOL_HANDSHAKE / TOOL_ACK) plus a resume token so downstream tool runners can rehydrate partial tool outputs after connection blips; streaming stability: introduce heartbeat sentinel frames and backoff-aware fragment coalescing to reduce duplicate fragments and improve reassembly across proxies.

Files changed (high level): api/compat/v1/param_normalizer.py (new) — canonicalization and migration shims; serving/streaming/framer.go — stop evaluation and heartbeat frames; runtime/tooling/handshake.go — tool handshake and resume token state machine; tests/compat/test_chat_stops.py — coverage for stop formats and streaming parity; tests/streaming/test_resume_reassembly.js — fuzz tests simulating partial reconnects; docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md — updated compatibility notes and migration guidance.

Commits (summary):
- 4f92d5d: add param normalizer and adapter glue;
- 9c1b3a7: implement streaming stop evaluation + heartbeat frames;
- a6e4b2f: tool handshake/resume protocol and runtime state;
- 2b7f113: tests, docs and CI flakiness fixes.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: existing clients should continue to work unchanged. Edge cases fixed: stop arrays passed as comma-separated single strings (legacy client bug) are normalized; stop handling differences between non-streamed and streamed codepaths are eliminated. Tool runners that rely on implicit stream termination should adopt the new handshake ACK semantics to avoid missing final fragments — see docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md for example pseudocode. No breaking API changes were made; developers wanting to opt into stricter stop-prioritization can set the new parameter "stop_mode=strict" (opt-in).

Tests and CI: added unit and integration tests that exercise mixed-mode streaming and reconnects; included a small synthetic latencies harness that revealed an off-by-one stop fence which was fixed. CI: build/test/lint all pass on main matrix except a transient macOS flake that required a rerun. Final CI status: pass.

Review thread (condensed): Reviewer Liam asked for clearer separation between param-normalizer side effects and request telemetry; I split the telemetry emission into a separate tracing hook as requested. Sofia requested an additional fuzz test for tool reassembly under packet reorder; added test case in tests/streaming/test_resume_reassembly.js. Eliot flagged a potential race in the resume token garbage collection; I added a bounded TTL and unit test. After two rounds of changes reviewers approved and marked ready.

Deployment notes: staged to canary and exercised against dedicated workloads; observed 0.4% p99 latency increase under large stop lists but 18% reduction in duplicate stream fragments. No rollout blockers.

Related work: references ENG-9384 (streaming parity effort) and ENG-9422 (tool-runner reliability). Links: internal design doc at /docs/design/chatv1-stop-tool-handshake.md and migration examples in docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md.

Release notes: "Improve v1 chat compatibility: consistent stop handling for streamed and sync responses; robust tool-call handshake with resume support to avoid lost tool outputs during reconnects; streaming stability improvements (heartbeat, fragment coalescing) and logprob envelope frames for clearer token-level diagnostics."
